readings: Join riskandmargin to orders on ordervault = recordvault and ignore unmatched records. For each non-null ordertune represented in the joined rows, count distinct matched orders. Compute the average of those counts across the represented order types. Among types whose counts exceed that average, return one row containing the average of their counts and the average of their counts minus that overall average, without rounding.

Join riskandmargin to orders on ordervault = recordvault and ignore unmatched records. For each non-null ordertune represented in the joined rows, count matching risk/margin records, counting an order once for each risk/margin record linked to it. Compute the average of those counts across the represented order types. Among types whose counts exceed that average, return one row containing the average of their counts and the average of their counts minus that overall average, without rounding.
queries:
WITH type_counts AS (
  SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) AS order_count
  FROM riskandmargin AS r
  JOIN orders AS o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault
  WHERE o.ordertune IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY o.ordertune
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(order_count) AS avg_count
  FROM type_counts
)
SELECT
  AVG(t.order_count),
  AVG(t.order_count - a.avg_count)
FROM type_counts AS t
CROSS JOIN overall AS a
WHERE t.order_count > a.avg_count

WITH type_counts AS (
  SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(*) AS risk_count
  FROM riskandmargin AS r
  JOIN orders AS o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault
  WHERE o.ordertune IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY o.ordertune
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(risk_count) AS avg_count
  FROM type_counts
)
SELECT
  AVG(t.risk_count),
  AVG(t.risk_count - a.avg_count)
FROM type_counts AS t
CROSS JOIN overall AS a
WHERE t.risk_count > a.avg_count
